title: Orchestrate run state, version 1
description: One orchestration of one ticket: the decisions the user gave at intake, the resolved lane plan, the cycle each stage is on, and what the loop has already acted on. It is what a resumed run reads instead of asking the user everything twice. It records no time budget, because the run has none.

decision_policy.description: Who answers when a stage would need the human. Resolved once at intake — the request's word over the profile's, else attended — and never changed midway: a resumed run resumes this policy.

decisions.description: Every decision comment a yolo run posted on the ticket, in order. Numbering continues across a resume, and the outcome comment lists them all so the run can be audited from the ticket alone.

handle.description: The live agent of this stage when the lane can keep one across cycles, so the next cycle resumes it with its context intact rather than starting fresh.

last_progress_at.description: When this run last OBSERVED progress from this stage — its announcement, a commit, a comment, a growing log, a live process. Never when it was last waited on: waiting is not progress. The stall check measures from here.

stall_checks.description: Stall checks run against the cycle currently in flight. Two consecutive checks finding no evidence of work mean the cycle is hung: stop it and spawn it again, which counts as an abnormal end.

relaunches.description: Consecutive abnormal ends of this stage. One is spawned again with the same brief; a second pauses the run for the user.

cycles.description: Cycles of this stage the run has spawned. A cycle is routing, not a relaunch: only an abnormal end counts toward relaunches.

progress.description: What the loop has read and acted on. Nothing watches: these are the results of this run's own reads between cycles.

next_cycle.description: The stage the pull request is owed next, decided from the last report and this run's own read.

unresolved_thread_sets.description: One sorted unresolved-thread-id set per Developer cycle that moved the head; three identical consecutive sets mean the loop is not converging and the run pauses for the user.

qa_failures.description: Scenario identifier to the number of times Manual QA has reported it failing. Three on one scenario pauses the run for the user.

pull_requests.description: The work set: one entry per open pull request the ticket governs, keyed OWNER/REPOSITORY#NUMBER, kept across the between-cycle re-reads. Each entry is that pull request's own position — every pull request keeps its own children, so its runs, cursor, and fingerprint never mix with another member's. An entry whose pull request closed or merged mid-run stays, with its lifecycle recorded, for the outcome comment.

parent.description: The set member whose head branch is this pull request's base branch, keyed the same way, when this pull request is a stacked child. The parent is worked first; this pull request's own Reviewer handles the base movement the parent causes.

stage_runs.description: Stage name to that stage's run identifier on this pull request, so resuming a cycle resumes this pull request's own runs, locks, and worktrees rather than another member's.

qa.description: This pull request's Manual QA evidence link or recorded waiver, for the outcome comment.

unresolved_thread_sets.description: As progress.unresolved_thread_sets, scoped to this pull request: the convergence test never mixes members of the set.

qa_failures.description: As progress.qa_failures, scoped to this pull request.

paused.description: The run is waiting for the user and holds everything it holds. It is not stopped: the answer goes into the next cycle's brief and the loop continues. Only an attended run pauses — under yolo the same moment becomes a posted decision, and the loop continues without a human.

reason.description: 'yolo-stop' is a decision this run took and posted with its reasoning before stopping — a clarity 'reconsider the work' it agreed with, or the same non-convergence condition tripping again after a yolo decision. A yolo run never stops on a question.
